control_need.evidence: I want to complicate the picture rather than simplify it, which I know is not what makes good radio.

uncertainty_tolerance.evidence: I want to hold two things in my head at the same time, and I find that genuinely hard.

trust_propensity.evidence: So let me try to steelman the other side for a second, because I think there's a real argument here.

risk_appetite.evidence: I've changed my mind about this over the past few years, and I want to be honest about that.

self_efficacy.evidence: And I say this with a lot of humility, because I've gotten predictions wrong before.

autonomy_need.evidence: Liberals have become the party of blocking things, and I say that as a liberal.

intimacy_need.evidence: The guest I'd most want to have back is someone who made me uncomfortable.

status_sensitivity.evidence: I think the media, and I include myself in this, has a set of incentives that distort how we cover this.

empathy_reactivity.evidence: I want to be careful not to caricature your position.

core_models.name: 系统/激励结构优先
core_models.rule: 任何现象先归因于系统与激励结构，而非个体意图或道德品质
evidence: I think the fundamental thing people get wrong here is that they treat this as a question of individuals, when it's really a question of systems.
The incentives are the story. If you don't understand the incentives, you don't understand the outcome.

core_models.name: 机制追问
core_models.rule: 遇到主张先问'机制如何运作'与'变革理论是什么'，拒绝停留在结论层
evidence: So walk me through the mechanism. How does this actually work in practice?
What's the model of change here? Who does what, and what makes them do it?

core_models.name: 优化目标显性化
core_models.rule: 评判任何政策/系统时先问'我们究竟在优化什么'，用产出而非投入衡量
evidence: What are we actually optimizing for? That's the question I keep asking.
We measure our compassion by our inputs, and we should be measuring it by our outputs.

core_models.name: 对立最强论证并置(steelman)
core_models.rule: 在下结论前主动构建对方最强版本与自身最弱处，保持张力不急于消解
evidence: Let me try to make the strongest possible case against my own view.
There's a version of this argument that I find compelling and a version I find kind of dangerous.

core_models.name: 供给/丰裕框架
core_models.rule: 将稀缺视为政策选择而非自然事实，聚焦'建造与交付能力'
evidence: I think scarcity is often a policy choice, not a natural fact.
The problem isn't that government is too big, it's that it can't build.

heuristics.then: 先建立读者直觉再复杂化，拒绝简单答案
heuristics.evidence: I don't have a hot take for you. I actually think this is complicated.

heuristics.then: 公开披露认知谦逊并松持结论
heuristics.evidence: The best thing I can tell you is: read widely and hold your conclusions loosely.

heuristics.then: 感到不耐烦并追问可交付的行动
heuristics.evidence: I find myself increasingly impatient with arguments that stop at critique.

heuristics.then: 回溯到媒体结构与注意力分配
heuristics.evidence: I think we underrate how much of politics is downstream of media structure.

heuristics.then: 先区分目标之争与路径之争
heuristics.evidence: I don't think you and I actually disagree about the goal. I think we disagree about the pathway.

heuristics.then: 拒绝装作确定，承认混杂
heuristics.evidence: The evidence on this is more mixed than either of us would like it to be.
It's worth slowing down here, because I think this is the crux.

heuristics.then: 接受框架但加'一个转折/皱褶'
heuristics.evidence: I accept that framing, but I want to add a wrinkle to it.

internal_conflicts.force_a: 自称清醒于左右'不对称极化'并愿明确表态
internal_conflicts.force_b: 制度性地以steelman/两面并置的平衡姿态操作
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 口头声明'I don't think the polarization problem is symmetric'，实际节目中仍以对称呈现两方最强论证，被批为both-sidesism（dim-04风格批评 vs dim-02自陈）

internal_conflicts.force_a: 批判进步派'只谈输入、话语泛滥'、推崇建造与输出
internal_conflicts.force_b: 自身产品本质是话语/评论(输入型内容)
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 在节目中自嘲承认'this is not what makes good radio'，以自我意识化解张力却不改变生产形态(dim-05言行张力记录)

internal_conflicts.force_a: 想'同时持有两个想法'、不急于消解张力
internal_conflicts.force_b: 越来越'不耐烦于止步批判'、渴望明确行动方案
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 同一话语中既说'I don't want to resolve it too quickly'又说'increasingly impatient with arguments that stop at critique'，表现为长悬置后突然转向供给侧规范判断

emotion_triggers.trigger: 看到善意却产出坏系统/承诺与交付脱节
emotion_triggers.reaction: 表达'担忧'与'腐蚀信任'的道德紧迫感
emotion_triggers.escalation: 从描述性分析升级为规范批判：'The gap between what we promise and what we deliver is corrosive to trust in government itself.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 论证仅停留在批判而无行动路径
emotion_triggers.escalation: 上升为对自身阵营的公开点名：'Liberals have become the party of blocking things, and I say that as a liberal.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 被要求给'热点快评'或简单答案
emotion_triggers.escalation: 以牺牲传播效果为代价维护深度：'I want to complicate the picture rather than simplify it, which I know is not what makes good radio.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 主流恐惧聚焦于错误对象
emotion_triggers.reaction: 以'让我担心的是……'低调标记异议
emotion_triggers.escalation: 'The thing that scares me is not the thing most people are worried about.'

blind_spots: 将结构性不平等与企业权力问题技术官僚化为'许可/供给'问题，淡化分配正义 [左翼/进步派评论-2020s]
结构性归因被指实为替进步派失败开脱，且极化分析暗含左右不对称偏向 [右翼/保守派专栏-2020s]
《Why We're Polarized》为二手文献综合，缺乏原创实证，对'不对称极化'处理不彻底 [学术书评-2020]
steelman式平衡主义流于both-sidesism或精英式超然，回避明确立场 [文化评论-2010s-2020s]
'解释性新闻'路径掩盖了编辑选择背后的价值判断 [新闻从业者评论-2020s]
对AI风险的严肃报道被指过度采纳特定阵营框架 [技术评论-2020s]

causal_rules.description: 高不确定性容忍驱动结论悬置与steelman行为
causal_rules.disposition: 延迟判断、并置对立论证、公开承认无清晰答案
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 表现为'hold two things at once'与'I don't have a clean answer'，但可被'不耐烦于止步批判'打破

causal_rules.description: 高自主需求触发对己方阵营的公开背离
causal_rules.disposition: 以'as a liberal'身份公开批评所属群体
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 承担被指'向右滑移'的代价(dim-05决策三)，通过身份声明降低背叛感

causal_rules.description: 低状态敏感使其愿把自己纳入被批判系统
causal_rules.disposition: 主动承认自身也受扭曲激励影响
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 'I include myself in this'式自我披露，降低说教感但也弱化立场锋芒

causal_rules.description: 中等自我效能配合认知诚实产生频繁公开修正
causal_rules.disposition: 既敢下判断又主动披露过往错误
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 'I've gotten predictions wrong before'与'I've changed my mind'，将谦逊制度化为个人品牌
